question: After the delivery-state defect is repaired, should generic tool-progress intent remain a supported public plugin SDK reply-payload contract?
rationale: Codex’s lifecycle supports the transient-versus-final distinction, but exposing a one-producer/one-channel-consumer contract to third-party plugins is a long-term compatibility choice that code correctness alone cannot settle.

options.title: Retain the generic public contract
options.body: Repair normal dispatch, add focused compatibility tests, and document the generic intent as the approved transport-neutral progress seam.

options.title: Keep progress intent bundled-only
options.body: Repair normal dispatch but move the metadata behind an internal or plugin-owned seam so external plugins do not gain a new compatibility contract.

options.title: Pause progress suppression
options.body: Do not merge the behavior until maintainers choose a durable owner boundary for transient progress presentation.

recommendation.title: Retain the generic public contract
recommendation.body: Repair normal dispatch, add focused compatibility tests, and document the generic intent as the approved transport-neutral progress seam.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision directly affects the recently authored Slack native-data delivery contract and the public plugin-facing behavior of that path.
